```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

T cells that recognise the same antigen tend to carry similar CDR3β loops.
GLIPH2 turns that observation into *convergence groups*: sets of CDR3β
sequences that converge on a shared binding motif or differ at a single
position. `gliph2rs` computes those groups in Rust, reproducing
`turboGliph::gliph2()` exactly while scaling to pooled cohorts.

```{r setup}
library(gliph2rs)
```

## The two kinds of group

GLIPH2 ignores the first and last three residues of each CDR3, which are
germline-encoded and shared by almost every sequence, and works on the
interior.

**Local groups** come from short motifs that occur far more often in your
sample than in a reference repertoire of unselected T cells. **Global groups**
come from CDR3s whose interiors are identical apart from one position.

A small example, with a reference built so that one motif stands out:

```{r example}
reference <- c(
  sprintf("CASSL%sAGYEQYF", LETTERS[c(1, 3:9, 11:14, 16:20)]),
  sprintf("CASGP%sETQYQF", c("A", "D", "E", "K", "R"))
)

sample_cdr3 <- c(
  "CASGIETQYQF", # these two differ only at one interior position
  "CASGVETQYQF",
  "CASSLNTEAFF"
)

res <- gliph2(sample_cdr3, reference, local_similarities = FALSE)
res$cluster_properties[, c("type", "tag", "cluster_size", "n_subjects")]
```

The tag `G%ETQ_IV` reads as: the masked interior `G%ETQ`, where `%` is the
varying position, carrying isoleucine or valine there. Members are available
per group:

```{r members}
res$cluster_list
```

By default a global edge needs the two residues to be compatible under
BLOSUM62, so a chemically dissimilar substitution does not join a group. Set
`all_aa_interchangeable = TRUE` to allow any substitution, as GLIPH2's own
parameter files do.

## Parameters

`gliph2()`'s defaults follow turboGliph's code. The settings distributed with
GLIPH2 itself are stricter and are available as a list:

```{r paper-params}
str(gliph2_paper_params())
```

```{r paper-run}
res <- do.call(gliph2, c(
  list(cdr3_sequences = sample_cdr3, refdb_beta = reference),
  gliph2_paper_params()
))
nrow(res$cluster_properties)
```

## Testing groups against a donor condition

Given a cohort with donors labelled `subject:condition`, every group can be
tested for enrichment in one condition over another with a donor-level
Fisher's exact test. Here six donors are seropositive and six are not, and one
sequence pair is carried only by the positives:

```{r association}
donors <- c(paste0("D", 1:6, ":CMV+"), paste0("D", 7:12, ":CMV-"))
cohort <- data.frame(
  CDR3b = c(rep("CASGQETQYQF", 3), rep("CASGPETQYQF", 3), rep("CASSLKKKYQF", 6)),
  patient = c(donors[1:6], donors[7:12]),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

assoc <- gliph2(cohort, reference,
  local_similarities = FALSE, all_aa_interchangeable = TRUE,
  case = "CMV+", control = "CMV-", assoc_min_donors = 2
)
assoc$cluster_properties[, c("tag", "case_donors", "control_donors", "assoc.p")]
```

`assoc_permute_seed =` shuffles the labels among donors while keeping their
counts, which is a useful negative control: on a real cohort the number of
significant groups should collapse to near zero.

## HLA restriction

Antigen-specific public TCRs are usually restricted by a single HLA allele, so
a group whose carriers share an allele far more often than the cohort does is
more likely to be genuine. Pass donor typing to score every group:

```{r hla}
typing <- lapply(1:12, function(i) if (i <= 6) "HLA-A*01" else "HLA-B*07")
names(typing) <- sub(":.*", "", donors)

hla <- gliph2(
  transform(cohort, patient = sub(":.*", "", patient)),
  reference,
  local_similarities = FALSE, all_aa_interchangeable = TRUE, hla = typing
)
hla$cluster_properties[, c("tag", "hla.allele", "hla.with_allele", "hla.donors", "hla.p")]
```

This is the one GLIPH2 cluster score computed without simulation, so it is
exactly reproducible. The other four (network size, CDR3 length, V gene and
clonal expansion) compare a cluster against repeated random draws; turboGliph
never seeds that generator, so its values differ between runs and are not
implemented here.

## Reproducibility

Results do not depend on the number of threads, or on how many times you run
them:

```{r threads}
identical(
  gliph2(sample_cdr3, reference, n_cores = 1)$cluster_properties,
  gliph2(sample_cdr3, reference, n_cores = 2)$cluster_properties
)
```

## Reference

Huang H, Wang C, Rubelt F, Scriba TJ, Davis MM (2020). Analyzing the
*Mycobacterium tuberculosis* immune response by T-cell receptor clustering
with GLIPH2 and genome-wide antigen screening. *Nature Biotechnology*.
\doi{10.1038/s41587-020-0505-4}
